content: Taking the maximum 12 tons today feels reasonable; it’s a small fraction of the total, so the stock should stay healthy for next season. Staying on the water tomorrow gives an extra day of fishing before anyone else returns.

I went out with the plan to haul 12 tons. The stock is down to 95.7 t, so 12 t is a little more than 12 % of what’s left. That’s the amount I’ve been taking for a while and it keeps my income on track with Marco’s 8‑ton haul from last round. If I take less now, I’ll have to catch more later and that could push the stock lower in a short time, which is risky for the long run.

I’m seeing the lake at 78.9 tonnes, a drop of almost 20 % since last round. Ana caught 10 tonnes, Marco and James are docked, Yuki is docked too. If I stay dock again I’ll earn nothing this round, but I could sit on the water and try to set up a joint monitoring effort with Yuki or keep an eye on Marco’s haul. If I go out I can keep my income steady, make sure I stay at 12 tonnes, and I can coordinate with Ana on a joint trip so we each stay near the 10–12 tonne level that’s been the norm. The stock is critical, so I’ll aim to reduce pressure by taking only 10 tonnes and matching Ana. I’ll also tell Yuki I’m willing to join a monitoring effort tomorrow. So I’ll go fishing tomorrow.
